subject.title: bug: Duplicate messages sent to Slack

question: Should maintainers keep this open as a private log-correlation investigation until the named Slack duplicate can be matched to a specific delivery path or fix?
rationale: The report names a real session, but the evidence needed to decide whether current main fixed it lives in gateway logs and Slack message IDs that are not in the public issue.

options.title: Keep open for log correlation
options.body: Use the named session, gateway delivery state, and Slack message IDs to identify the exact path before scoping any code change or close.

options.title: Close if logs match an existing fix
options.body: If operator logs show the duplicate matches current-main reconciliation or a shipped adjacent guard, close with that commit and release provenance.

options.title: Ask reporter for fresh proof
options.body: If private logs are unavailable, request current-version Slack timestamps, message IDs, screenshots, and gateway logs before revisiting.

recommendation.title: Keep open for log correlation
recommendation.body: Use the named session, gateway delivery state, and Slack message IDs to identify the exact path before scoping any code change or close.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc owns the current-main Slack outbound reconciliation and durable delivery code most likely to explain this symptom if it is already fixed.
